In the Go repo at /bench/repo (the "memos" project, indexed in codebase-memory-mcp as project "memos"), answer with exact path:line citations. Search breadth: very thorough.

Q1 (h02): The server can notify external systems over HTTP when content changes (webhooks). Find where the outbound HTTP delivery actually executes (the function doing http.Post/client.Do), its file path. Then find what protects it from SSRF / being pointed at internal network addresses (e.g. URL validation, IP blocklist of private ranges, dial control) and cite path:lines. If no protection exists, verify thoroughly (check the webhook plugin/package, URL validation on webhook creation) and say so.

Q2 (h06): Which gRPC/RPC API handler methods (in server/router/api/... service implementations) can TRANSITIVELY cause an outbound HTTP request to a user-configured webhook URL? Trace call chains: handler → ... → webhook dispatch → HTTP post. Name at least three handler methods (e.g. CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, UpsertMemoReaction, etc. — verify which actually do), and identify the single function where these paths converge before delivery (name + path:line). Use trace_path or grep for calls to the dispatch function.

Q3 (r04): Is there ANY message broker (NATS, RabbitMQ, Kafka, any queue) involved in webhook delivery? Search go.mod and code. Describe the actual delivery mechanism (e.g. synchronous call or goroutine) with path:line.

Return concise findings with citations.

content.text:
## Q1 — Outbound HTTP delivery + SSRF protection

**Delivery point:** `webhook.Post` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-180`, actual wire call at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152` (`safeClient.Do(req)`). Request built at `:126`, HMAC-SHA256 "Standard Webhooks" signing headers at `:133-150`.

**SSRF protection exists, in two layers:**

1. **Dial-time IP blocking (defeats DNS rebinding / TOCTOU).** The shared client is pinned to a custom transport: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:29-37` (`safeClient` with `DialContext: safeDialContext`, 30s timeout at `:27`). `safeDialContext` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77` resolves the host and rejects the connection if **any** resolved IP is reserved (`:70-74`). Note it dials `net.JoinHostPort(host, port)` (`:76`), i.e. re-resolves rather than pinning the checked IP — a narrow residual rebinding window, but the check is at dial time so it is far tighter than validate-only.

2. **Creation-time URL validation.** `webhook.ValidateURL` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83`: absolute-URL parse (`:63`), http/https scheme allowlist (`:67-69`), DNS resolution + reserved-range rejection (`:71-81`). Blocklist of private ranges: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23` (loopback, RFC-1918 ×3, 169.254.0.0/16 incl. cloud IMDS, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10), parsed once in `init` at `:28-36`; membership test `isReservedIP` at `:44-54`.

Enforced on the API surface at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74` (CreateUserWebhook) and `:161`, `:182` (UpdateUserWebhook paths), plus signing-secret validation at `:86`, `:170`, `:190`.

**Escape hatch:** `AllowPrivateIPs` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:38-41`) short-circuits `isReservedIP` at `:45`. It is only ever assigned in tests (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook_test.go:91`, `:142`) — no flag/env/config wires it, so it is `false` in production.

Only other `client.Do` in non-test Go code is unrelated OAuth2 (`/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:91`). No second/legacy webhook plugin package exists (`internal/webhook/` is the only one; no `plugin/` dir).

## Q2 — Handlers that transitively reach webhook delivery

**Convergence point: `webhook.PostAsync` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`** (all paths funnel here; it feeds the queue consumed by workers that call `Post` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:46`).

Six handler methods reach it:

| Handler | Definition | Dispatch call site |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` | `:157` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` |
| `UpdateMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` | `:513` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` |
| `DeleteMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` | `:562` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` | `:119` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16` | `:48` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` |
| `SetMemoRelations` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16` | `:48` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` |

Intermediate hops: `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:66-78` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:20` → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:48-74` → `webhook.PostAsync` at `:71`. The comment path calls `PostAsync` directly at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43`.

**Verified negative:** reaction handlers (`UpsertMemoReaction` / `DeleteMemoReaction`) do **not** dispatch webhooks — no `Webhook`/`PostAsync` references in `memo_reaction*.go`. Also note the MCP router exposes `MemoService_CreateMemo`, `MemoService_UpdateMemo`, `MemoService_CreateMemoComment` as tools (`/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/catalog.go:13-18`), giving a second entry point into the same handlers.

## Q3 — No message broker

No NATS/RabbitMQ/AMQP/Kafka/Redis/asynq/NSQ/SQS/Pulsar dependency in `/bench/repo/go.mod` or anywhere in Go source (the only `segmentio` entries are `asm`/`encoding`, indirect JSON deps; other grep hits were SQL test helpers).

**Actual mechanism: an in-process buffered Go channel with a fixed worker pool.**
- Queue: `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`
- Workers: 4 goroutines started in package `init`, each draining the channel and calling `Post` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`
- Producer: non-blocking `select` with `default` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:189-195`; **when the queue is full the webhook is silently dropped** (warn-logged only, `:192-195`). Nil payloads are also dropped (`:185-188`).

So delivery is fire-and-forget, at-most-once, in-memory only: no persistence, no retry, and pending deliveries are lost on process restart. Handlers are non-blocking with respect to the HTTP POST, but errors from dispatch enumeration (store lookups) are still returned/logged synchronously at the call sites listed in Q2.
